newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Fiat launches Siena model from Argentina to world.
newsitem.headline: Fiat launches Siena model from Argentina to world.

text.p: Italian automaker Fiat SpA launched late Monday from Argentina its compact model Siena for world markets and said it expects to increase production to more than 120,000 next year.
At the same time, the company presented in Argentina the compact Palio, the second best-selling car in Brazil, where it started production of it last year.

In Argentina, the Siena and Palio are made in Cordoba province, 700 km (400 miles) northwest of Buenos Aires, in a $600 million plant inaugurated in December and familiarly known in the company as 'Little Melfi,' after the state-of-the art plant in Southern Italy.

"For the first time, Argentina is the launching platform of a car, the Fiat Siena, built in this country and intended for the international markets," President of Fiat Auto Argentina Cristiano Rattazzi told hundreds of journalists.
"Argentina is the perfect country for the launch," he added, underlying economic growth and virtually no inflation.

Giovanni Razelli, Fiat general director for Latin America, said the firm this year aimed to sell 560,000 Sienas, Palios and other models in the customs unions Mercosur and the number is expected to increase to more than 750,000 by the year 2000.
Mercosur is formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
The Siena is aimed at middle to upper income drivers, while the Palio is intended for younger motorists or as a second car.
Prices will be announced later this week.

In the face of a mature market in Western Europe, Japan and the United States, a group of countries are emerging where the car sector is steadily growing, he said, adding growth of more than 70 percent is foreseen in South America, Asia and Eastern Europe.

In 1989, Fiat sold 61 percent of its cars in Italy, 32 percent in the rest of Europe and only seven percent in the rest of the world while in 1996 those percentages were 34, 32 and 34, respectively, officials said.
The Cordoba plant has an initial capacity of 120,000 vehicles per year, which will rise to 200,000 at a later stage.
Together with its plant in the Brazilian city of Betim, the Cordoba plant, which has 5,000 workers, constitutes the industrial base of the company in Latin America.
In 1997, Fiat plans to produce 65,000 Sienas in Argentina, half of them for export to Brazil. In 1998, it will make 128,000, half of them to be sold abroad.
Between 1982 and July 1996, Fiat cars were made in Argentina by Sevel, also a licensee of Peugeot. Fiat now manufactures its own cars in Argentina.
